meta.probingQuestion: How do you use your strength without taking someone else's?

games.title: Half Guard with Standing Transition Game

meta.connection: You can have full control of someone's back and still choose not to hurt them. That is the whole system: the power to hurt, and the choice not to. Using your strength for people instead of over them is that same choice, made in your life.
meta.takeaway: Tonight you worked from an underhook tie, half guard, and back control. You can have full control of someone's back and still choose not to hurt them, and that choice is the whole point. Using your strength for people, instead of over them, is that same choice made off the mat. You get to hold real power and still choose mercy.

slides.title: How do you use your strength without taking someone else's?

body.text: This is tripping a standing player by blocking his foot.

items: The overhook player wins when the underhook player falls onto his own hips or hands.
The underhook player wins by closing his own hands under the overhook player's elbows.

body.text: Half Guard with Standing Transition Game
This is getting close to a partner on his back.

items: The bottom player wins by getting his feet inside and sitting up, or entangling the top player once he stands.
The top player wins by locking his hands.

body.text: This is holding him from behind with your chest on his back.

items: The top player holds as long as he keeps contact.
The bottom player wins by getting his back to the mat or turning face to face.

slides.question: You've got an overhook, and you've just made foot-to-foot contact with your partner. What's the smart move?

options.text: Stick that foot and pull for the sweep.

options.text: Let go of the foot contact and reset.
options.feedback: Letting go here gives up ground you just built.

options.text: Grab for his head instead of his foot.
